title: The Exercises list goes through every set ever logged each time it opens, to show when each exercise was last done
what: Each visit to Profile, Exercises works out 'Last: 12 Oct' for every exercise by grouping every set the member has ever saved and joining each to its workout. After an import of five years (about 32,000 sets) this read grows with the whole history and is not part of the timed speed check.
expected: The last-done day is kept up to date when a workout is saved, or read from a short index, so opening the list costs the same in year five as in week one.
who: members with long or imported history
how_often: every visit to the Exercises list
fix_line: Read the last-done days from a small index or keep them updated on save, and add the list to the speed check

title: The five-years-of-data speed check is never run automatically and has no time limit
what: A speed check that loads a made-up five-year history and times every member action exists, but the normal test run skips it, no cloud workflow runs it, and it only prints times without failing on any. A change that makes the workout screen or History slow with long history would pass every check.
expected: The long-history speed check runs in the cloud on each change and fails when a key action (start a workout, open History, open an exercise) reads far more rows or statements than its recorded budget.
fix_line: Run the long-history speed check in the cloud and fail on a statement or row-count budget

title: Routines and their exercises have no index for which folder or routine they belong to
what: The routine tables are looked up by folder and by routine on every routine open, reorder, move and delete, and deleting a folder or routine clears its exercises through the same link, but none of these links has an index, so each lookup goes through the whole table. The tables are small (tens of routines), so members will not feel it today.
expected: The routine-to-folder and exercise-to-routine links have an index, like the workout and set tables already do.
fix_line: Add the two missing indexes to the start-up index list
